items.title: tableprinter: IsTTY conflates padding with truncation, so aligned output is impossible on non-TTYs
items.body:
### Problem

`TablePrinter` computes correct column widths for every cell, then discards them
unless `IsTTY` is true. On a non-TTY it emits unpadded values joined by tabs,
leaving alignment to the consumer's tab stops. Rendered at 8-column tab stops —
what a terminal and the GitLab job-log viewer both do — columns don't line up:

```
PACKAGE VERSION STATUS  REASON
@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin        8.18.0  Blocked policy violation
lodash  4.17.21 Warning deprecated
```

`VERSION` starts at column 8 on one row and column 40 on another.

This is deliberate for piped/scripted use, added in `e5cf7c314`
("scriptability: Avoid truncating columns of tables/lists on non-TTYs",
resolves #706). The gap is that #706 only asked for **truncation** to be
disabled on non-TTYs, and the implementation disabled **padding** as well —
both sit behind the same guard:

```go
// internal/tableprinter/table_printer.go:269
if c.Width > 0 && c.isaTTY {
    ...
    return text.Truncate(s, c.Width)  // Truncate() is also what pads
}
return s                               // non-TTY: no padding either
```

So there's no way to ask for *aligned but untruncated* output — which is exactly
what a CI job log needs: a human reader, no terminal width to respect. Any
command wanting that has to hand-roll its own column math.

**Secondary issue:** on the TTY path, cells are padded *and* joined with `"\t"`,
so a padded cell followed by a tab jumps to the next 8-column stop. With
`TerminalWidth = 80`, `colWidths` budgets a 62-column line that renders as 72 —
the width capping is computed against a width that isn't what gets printed.
Padding and tab separators shouldn't both apply.

### Suggested fix

Separate the two concerns — e.g. a `Pad bool` independent of `IsTTY`, or pad
whenever widths are known and gate only truncation on `IsTTY`. Commands
rendering human-facing output in CI opt into padding; piped list commands keep
today's TSV contract unchanged. Dropping the tab separator when padding is
active would fix the width discrepancy at the same time.

### Repro

```go
tp := tableprinter.NewTablePrinter()
tp.IsTTY = false // or true, to see the width overshoot
tp.TerminalWidth = 80
tp.AddRow("PACKAGE", "VERSION", "STATUS", "REASON")
tp.AddRow("@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin", "8.18.0", "Blocked", "policy violation")
tp.AddRow("lodash", "4.17.21", "Warning", "deprecated")
fmt.Print(tp.Render()) // pipe through `expand -t8`
```

items.title: glab fails when the remote uses the instance's separate SSH hostname, such as ssh.gitlab.gnome.org
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: glab 1.126.0 (4dd0d32d1)
- [x] Operating system and version: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.2.8, x86_64)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? self-managed (gitlab.gnome.org)
- [x] GitLab version (if self-managed): 19.4.5
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues: logged in to gitlab.gnome.org
- [x] Run the command in debug mode: `GLAB_DEBUG=true` only adds a telemetry hook line repeating the same error

### Summary

In a clone whose remote is on `ssh.gitlab.gnome.org`, every repository command fails with "none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitLab host", although glab is logged in to gitlab.gnome.org. The error says to run `glab auth login`, which was already done.

gitlab.gnome.org serves Git over SSH on that separate hostname, and glab only matches a remote on it to the instance when `ssh_host` is set for the instance.

`glab auth login` only sets it with `--ssh-hostname` or when run interactively inside the clone, so a scripted login, or one done before cloning, leaves it unset.

Workaround: `glab config set ssh_host ssh.gitlab.gnome.org --host gitlab.gnome.org`.

### Environment

- OS: Linux 7.2.8-1-t2-resolute x86_64 (Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS)
- SHELL: /bin/bash
- TERM: xterm-ghostty
- GLAB: glab 1.126.0 (4dd0d32d1)

Other:

### Steps to reproduce

1. `glab auth login --hostname gitlab.gnome.org --stdin < token.txt`
2. `git clone git@ssh.gitlab.gnome.org:GNOME/gnome-settings-daemon.git && cd gnome-settings-daemon`
3. `glab issue list`

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

```plaintext
none of the git remotes configured for this repository point to a known GitLab host. Please use `glab auth login` to authenticate and configure a new host for glab.

Configured remotes: ssh.gitlab.gnome.org.
```

### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

glab lists the issues of `GNOME/gnome-settings-daemon` on gitlab.gnome.org, as it does with the workaround.

### Possible fixes

In [`remote_resolver.go`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/blob/c2544a916/internal/cmdutils/remote_resolver.go#L141-155), map an SSH host that is a subdomain of a configured host to that host, unless an `ssh_host` says otherwise. The test "SSH host matches but no ssh_host config — remote skipped" asserts the current behavior; I found no discussion in !2924 that made it deliberate.

I have a merge request ready for this.

items.title: `glab release create` wipes release notes when updating an existing release without `--notes`
items.body:
<!---
Please read this!

Before opening a new issue, make sure to search for keywords in the issues
filtered by the "bug" label:

- https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/issues/?label_name%5B%5D=type%3A%3Abug

and verify the issue you're about to submit isn't a duplicate.
--->

### Checklist

<!-- Please test the latest versions, that will remove the possibility that you see a bug that is fixed in a newer version. -->

- [x] I'm using the latest version of the extension (Run `glab --version`)
  - Extension version: v1.126.0
- [x] Operating system and version: Done via docker in CI (job using `registry.gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli:latest`)
- [x] Gitlab.com or self-managed instance? _gitlab.com
- [ ] GitLab version (if self-managed) _GitLab version here_
  (Use the `version` endpoint, like this: gitlab.my-company.com/api/v4/version) 
- [x] I have performed `glab auth status` to check for authentication issues
- [ ] Run the command in debug mode (like `GLAB_DEBUG=true glab mr list`) and attach any useful output

### Summary

Updating an existing release with `glab release create` without passing `--notes` / `--notes-file` clears the release description.

The command help documents this as a supported way to update a release without changing its notes:

```shell
# Update an existing release (e.g., change the release date) without modifying notes
glab release create v1.0.1 --released-at "2024-01-15T10:00:00Z"
```

In practice, it seems that the update request sends `"description": null`, and GitLab clears the release notes.

This looks like a regression from !2918 (fix for #8193), which made notes optional on update.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a release with notes:

   ```shell
   glab release create 1.0.0 --notes "Some release notes" --name 1.0.0
   ```

2. Update only the release date, as shown in the help text:

   ```shell
   glab release create 1.0.0 --released-at "2026-10-30T10:00:00Z"
   ```

3. Look at the release. The description is now empty.


### Environment

Other: This is being ran via a CI job within Docker using the glab official image

### Steps to reproduce

<!-- How one can reproduce the issue - this is very important -->

### What is the current _bug_ behavior?

The `PUT /projects/:id/releases/:tag_name` request sent by glab includes `"description": null`:

```
PUT /api/v4/projects/g%2Fp/releases/1%2E0%2E0
{"name":"1.0.0","description":null,"released_at":"2026-10-30T10:00:00Z"}
```

(Captured by running glab v1.126.0 against a local HTTP server that logs requests.)

GitLab treats `description: null` as "set the description to empty", so the existing release notes are deleted.


### What is the expected _correct_ behavior?

When `--notes` / `--notes-file` is not provided on update, `description` should be left out of the request body entirely, so the existing release notes are kept, as the help text describes:

```
{"name":"1.0.0","released_at":"2026-10-30T10:00:00Z"}
```


### Relevant logs and/or screenshots

CI job output from the update step (the release had notes before this ran and had none afterwards):

```
$ glab release create "${CI_COMMIT_TAG}" --released-at "${RELEASE_DATE}"
• Validating tag 75.33.0
• Creating or updating release repo=<group>/<project> tag=75.33.0
✓ Release updated	url=https://gitlab.com/<group>/<project>/-/releases/75.33.0
✓ Release succeeded after 0.70 seconds.
```


### Possible fixes

glab only sets the description when notes were provided (`internal/commands/release/create/create.go`):

```go
updateOpts := &gitlab.UpdateReleaseOptions{
    Name: &opts.Name,
}
if opts.notes != "" {
    updateOpts.Description = &opts.notes
}
```

But `UpdateReleaseOptions` in `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go/v3` (v3.39.1, as pinned by glab v1.126.0) has no `omitempty` on `Description`, so a `nil` pointer is still serialised as `null`:

```go
type UpdateReleaseOptions struct {
    Name        *string    `url:"name" json:"name"`
    Description *string    `url:"description" json:"description"`
    Milestones  *[]string  `url:"milestones,omitempty" json:"milestones,omitempty"`
    ReleasedAt  *time.Time `url:"released_at,omitempty" json:"released_at,omitempty"`
}
```

Possible fixes:

- Add `omitempty` to `Description` (and probably `Name`) in `client-go`'s `UpdateReleaseOptions`, then bump `client-go` in glab.
- Or, until then, have glab fetch the existing release and send its current description back when no notes are provided.

A test asserting that the update request body has no `description` key when notes aren't provided would stop this from coming back.
